doc.title: Charles Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Playing with young Herbie Hancock and the live 'Impact' recording
summary: Hancock and Tolliver were close in age; the 1972 'Impact' record with Alvin Queen was a live date at the Domicile in Munich.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: I see. Well I’m struck by the fact that you mentioned showing up for this rehearsal and oh my God, there’s Roy Haynes and Herbie Hancock, who actually was only — fairly close to age to you. And I just find it so interesting —
Well he was 24, 23, 24. And me 21 or 22 you know.

Yeah. Very exciting. So I was listening to something from a record you did years later in ’72, it happened to have one of my favorite drummers Alvin Queen on it, and the record was “Impact.” And I’m curious if the rehearsal time and recording time, how it compared to your first experience with Jackie McLean. Did you have more time, less time?
Well that was a live recording.

I mean you know, I was heavily touring that band you know, during that period, especially in Europe. And we were at this famous club at the time called The Domicile in Munich. And that’s where we recorded that.
And Alvin is in Switzerland now.
